children: Vancouver, British Columbia – TheNewswire – October 13, 2026 – Solid Impact Investments Corp. (TSXV: SOLI.P) ("Solid" or the "Company"), a capital pool company, announces that it has adopted a semi-annual financial reporting ("SAR") framework, effective immediately. This change is being made pursuant to the Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers ("CBO 51-933").
CBO 51-933 allows eligible venture issuers to voluntarily move from a quarterly to a semi-annual financial reporting framework.

Transition Details – Solid’s fiscal year ends on May 31. Under the SAR framework, the Company will be exempt from filing interim financial reports and related Management Discussion & Analysis (“MD&A”) for its first and third quarters for so long as it continues to meet eligibility criteria under CBO 51-933.
By adopting the SAR, Solid aims to reduce the administrative and financial burden associated with quarterly reporting, allowing management to focus resources on advancement of different projects.
Initial Interim Period: The Company will not file an interim report for the first quarter (Q1) ending August 31, 2026 and for the third quarter (Q3) ending February 28, 2027.

Ongoing Reporting: Solid will continue to file audited annual consolidated financial statements (due within 120 days of May 31, 2027), and six-month interim financial reports (due within 60 days of November 30, 2026).
Continued Disclosure: The Company remains committed to timely disclosure and will continue to report all material changes and significant developments as required under National Instrument 51-102.

Eligibility: Solid confirms it meets the pilot program's eligibility criteria, which includes being a venture issuer with annual revenues of less than $10 million and maintaining a clean 12-month continuous disclosure record.
Continued Participation: Should the Company cease to continue participating in the SAR Pilot Program, it will announce it in a future news release
